title: 5am Club
logline: A trail runner walks us through the eight quiet steps between his 4:58 alarm and a ridge-top sunrise. Step four, always before the headlamp goes on, is {product}.

world.setting: A small one-bedroom apartment at the edge of a mountain town in the fictional Pinecrest Valley, 4:58am in late September, then the fictional Larch Ridge trail above town at sunrise.
world.palette: Indoors: warm oak, cream walls, black accents, amber lamp light against deep blue-hour windows, so the cool silver and sky-blue can is the coolest thing in the room. Outdoors: blue dawn turning to gold on silver-grey granite.
fictional_brands: Larch Ridge Trail (never shown as text; the trail marker is a plain orange diamond)
Pinecrest Valley (town, never shown as text)
world.rules: Shoes, running vest, headlamp and clothes are plain with no logos. Fridge holds glass jars and plain unlabelled cartons only. The phone alarm is face down or a plain glow; the time is added in post. Every sign and label is blank.

beats.summary: In bed at 4:58 with the phone glowing, he whispers to the tripod: five am, come run with me.
Steps one to three at a clip: feet on the cold floor, a big glass of water at the dark window, the double knot.
Step four slows down: the fridge light on the can, then the crack and a sip at the counter, with the name and the benefit.
Steps five to seven speed up again: the headlamp clicks on, the door opens into the blue dark, the climb by headlamp beam.
Step eight: the ridge at sunrise, headlamp off, the valley in cloud below.
Back to the fridge door: step four waiting for the viewer, with the tagline.

lore: Wes Tanaka works the repair counter at the only bike shop in Pinecrest Valley, which opens at 9. If the ridge is going to happen, it happens before work.

He is in week 12 of a 16-week plan for his first 50k, the Larch Ridge Ultra on the second Saturday of October. The plan is a hand-drawn grid taped to the fridge, eleven rows crossed out in black marker.
He has topped Larch Ridge 147 times and brings one small grey stone down from the summit cairn each time. The jar by the sink is nearly full.
He has rented the one-bedroom above a closed hardware store for six years. The radiator clanks for the first time each autumn, and it started this week.
Miso, a 14-year-old grey tabby, sleeps on the arm of the couch and does not get up for anyone before 7.
